verbalization: Idelalisib, a phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor, is known to be used in the treatment of Acute Lymphoblastic/lymphocytic Leukemia (ALL), a type of cancer that affects B-cells. The evidence suggests that Idelalisib may be repurposed for Neoplasm Of Mature B-cells, as it is indicated for ALL and the indication for Bendamustine, which is used in the treatment of Neoplasm Of Mature B-cells. This implies a potential pathway where Idelalisib could exert its therapeutic effects on B-cell malignancies, possibly through inhibition of the PI3K pathway, which is frequently dysregulated in B-cell neoplasms. The integration of these indications suggests a possible link between Idelalisib and the treatment of mature B-cell neoplasms, though further mechanistic studies are needed to confirm this relationship.
